title: A `[limits]` value that is not a quantity, or a global one above its `[limits.hard]` ceiling, boots and runs uncapped.
text: `rule:config/one-parser-for-the-boot-path-and-config-set` says the boot refuses a value that is not a quantity, and `rule:config/ceilings-are-their-own-directives` says the enforceable per-request cap is the `[limits.hard]` ceiling. `nvs config check` answers `ok` for `[limits] memory = "12 bananas"` and for `[limits] memory = "1G"` under `[limits.hard] memory = "512M"`, and `nvs run` under either config builds a 600 MiB string that the default 128 MiB ceiling refuses. The resolve bounds `[app.limits]` against the global ceiling (`crates/nvs-config/src/app.rs:134`) and the two body caps against theirs (`crates/nvs-config/src/resolve.rs:495`), and its doc declines the global start above the global ceiling as incoherent but bounded (`crates/nvs-config/src/app.rs:124`); the probe shows it is not bounded. The tree leaves a malformed size to the place sizes are parsed (`crates/nvs-config/src/tree.rs:16`), and the runtime reads a malformed `memory` or `max_output` as no cap at all (`crates/nvs-runtime/src/ctx/limits.rs:959`, its doc at `:912`), so the value is never refused anywhere. Closing it means the resolve refuses every `[limits]` and `[limits.hard]` quantity that does not parse as `E0601`, and a global `[limits]` value above a written `[limits.hard]` as `body_caps` already does for its two keys, each with a case under `nvs config check` and `nvs run`.
